name: Offline write-buffer
purpose: Owns the buffering and reconciliation contract for writes attempted while navigator.onLine is false. Every buffered write carries an idempotency token, a serialised payload and a monotonic sequence; on reconnection the buffer flushes in sequence and the server dedupes on the idempotency token.
responsibilities: Persist every buffered write to the applied local buffer (IndexedDB by default per ADR-2303, an elicited alternative for projects that need it) with an idempotency token, serialised payload and sequence (AC-22105-1).
Expose window.__offlineBuffer as a read-only enumeration for the pack and for project-side smoke tests (AC-22105-1).
Announce buffered-write count changes through the polite live-region wrapper on entry and on reconnection (AC-22105-1 via TAC-2301).
On reconnection, flush the buffer in sequence, retain the entry on flush failure with a retry counter, and clear the entry on flush success.
internalStructure: One buffer module the state machine invokes on offline entry and exit. The buffer wraps the applied storage engine (default IndexedDB via a small adapter interface, elicited alternatives per ADR-2303) with a serialise/deserialise pair and a monotonic counter. The reconciliation loop is idempotent: replaying the flush against the same buffer produces the same server-side effect.

interfaces.name: bufferWrite
interfaces.description: bufferWrite({ payload, idempotencyToken }) -> { sequence }. Persists the write, returns the sequence assigned. The idempotency token is caller-supplied so the server-side dedupe key is stable across retries.

interfaces.name: flushBuffer
interfaces.description: flushBuffer({ onSuccess, onFailure }) -> { flushed, retained }. Called on reconnection; iterates the buffer in sequence, calling onSuccess or onFailure per entry.

dependencies.name: State machine
dependencies.description: The state machine dispatches offline entry and reconnection into this buffer.

tradeoffs: IndexedDB by default is available in every modern browser but requires the applied surface to run in a browser context (not a WebView with a locked-down storage policy). Projects on a stripped WebView elicit an alternative via ADR-2303. Retention semantics on flush failure are per-write; a global give-up threshold is a project-side concern and not part of the v1 contract.
notes: The buffer is a runtime-observable contract; the pack drives an offline probe with a synthetic write and asserts window.__offlineBuffer is populated.
